text: Gulls flew near the boat. <break time="0.8s" /> Or sat on the water like ducks. <break time="0.8s" /> And they stared at the men. <break time="0.8s" /> With black, bead like eyes. <break time="0.8s" /> One gull came down. <break time="0.8s" /> And tried to land. <break time="0.8s" /> On the captains head. <break time="0.8s" /> But he did not dare. <break time="0.8s" /> To strike at it. <break time="0.8s" /> With the heavy rope. <break time="0.8s" /> Any sudden movement. <break time="0.8s" /> Could have turned the boat over so the captain gently waved. <break time="0.8s" /> The bird away with his hand. <break time="0.8s" /> The oiler and the correspondent. <break time="0.8s" /> Took turns at the oars. <break time="0.8s" /> And changing seats in that small boat. <break time="0.8s" /> Was harder than stealing eggs. <break time="0.8s" /> From under a hen. <break time="0.8s" /> So carefully did they move. <break time="0.8s" /> That the boat hardly rocked. <break time="0.8s" /> And each man rowed. <break time="0.8s" /> Until his back and arms ached. <break time="0.8s" /> Late in the morning. <break time="0.8s" /> The captain raising himself in the bow. <break time="0.8s" /> Said that he could see. <break time="0.8s" /> The lighthouse at Mosquito Inlet. <break time="0.8s" /> The correspondent who was rowing. <break time="0.8s" /> Had to turn his head many times. <break time="0.8s" /> Before he finally found. <break time="0.8s" /> The tiny thing on the horizon. <break time="0.8s" /> It looked like the point of a pin. <break time="0.8s" /> And yet it showed the men. <break time="0.8s" /> That land was really out there.
